issues.legal_issue: A partnership firm cannot be sued in its firm name in an eviction proceeding to which the ordinary civil procedure rules do not apply.
material_facts: An eviction application under a rent-control order was brought against a partnership firm in the firm name.
The civil procedure rules did not apply to proceedings under that rent-control order.
issues.conclusion: The firm could not be sued in its firm name in the eviction application because the civil procedure provision permitting suit against a firm by its firm name did not apply.
issues.legal_principle: A firm is a compendious name for its partners and has no separate capacity to be sued in its firm name unless the applicable procedure permits it. Order 30 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits a firm to sue and be sued in its own name, but that Code did not apply to proceedings under the rent-control order.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding seeks eviction under a rent-control regime.
predicates.partnership_firm_named_as_respondent: The respondent is identified as a partnership by its firm name.
predicates.ordinary_civil_procedure_does_not_apply: The ordinary civil procedure rules do not govern the proceeding.
predicates.partnership_firm_cannot_be_sued_in_firm_: A partnership cannot be sued in its firm name in the proceeding.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding is governed by rent-control procedure, a partnership is named as respondent by its firm name, and ordinary civil procedure does not apply, the partnership cannot be sued in that name.

issues.legal_issue: Naming a partnership firm instead of its partners in an eviction application is a correctable misdescription when the partners are before the court under the firm name.
material_facts: The eviction application named the partnership firm rather than its individual partners.
The partners were before the court under the firm name, although they had been described incorrectly.
The respondent sought to amend the application to add the partners as respondents and make consequential amendments.
issues.conclusion: The defect was a misdescription that could be corrected at any stage, rather than a ground to dismiss the application. The amendment adding the partners was allowed, and the case was remitted for determination on the merits.
issues.legal_principle: Where the partners are before the court under the firm name, the incorrect description is a misdescription that may be corrected at any stage; it does not by itself require dismissal. No earlier cases are relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding seeks eviction under a rent-control regime.
predicates.partnership_named_in_firm_name: The application identifies the partnership by its firm name instead of naming its partners individually.
predicates.partners_before_court_under_firm_name: The partners are before the court under the firm name, although not individually named.
predicates.misdescription_can_be_corrected_without_: The incorrect description may be corrected without dismissing the application.

issues.definition: If a rent-control eviction application names a partnership by its firm name and its partners are before the court under that name, the description can be corrected without dismissal.
